title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LAMAR'S TURKEY
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lamar Pettiford, a pool cleaner in Tucson, Arizona.
He offered to host Thanksgiving for his wife Gina's whole family, twelve people from Chicago.
Lamar had never cooked anything bigger than a hot dog.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: TOO PROUD
segments.quote: Many things are lost for want of asking.
segments.author: Old English proverb
lines: Too proud to admit it, he watched cooking videos until two a.m. and got more confused.
Then he saw the dish towel his mom sent from Memphis:
Many things are lost for want of asking.
So he called his mom, the butcher, and the lady at the grocery store.
By Sunday, he had a plan and a roasting pan.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FROZEN BIRD
segments.quote: It is common sense to take a method and try it. If it fails, admit it frankly and try another. But above all, try something.
segments.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
lines: Thanksgiving morning, the turkey was still frozen, hard as a bowling ball.
Gina, a history buff, read him President Franklin Roosevelt:
It is common sense to take a method and try it. If it fails, admit it frankly and try another. But above all, try something.
A cold bath in the tub was too slow. So he tried another, and bought two fresh turkey breasts.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: POOL BOY
segments.quote: Kindness is in our power, even when fondness is not.
segments.author: Samuel Johnson
lines: At noon, Gina's dad Frank walked in. Retired Chicago firefighter. Hey, Pool Boy. Where's the turkey?
Lamar wanted to snap back. Then he remembered his grandpa's line from the English writer Samuel Johnson:
Kindness is in our power, even when fondness is not.
So he gave Frank the best chair, a cold root beer, and the remote.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: LUMPY GRAVY
segments.quote: If I am walking with two other men, each of them will serve as my teacher.
segments.author: Confucius
lines: Then the gravy went lumpy.
Frank wandered in. He'd made gravy for twenty firefighters every Sunday.
Lamar remembered the old Chinese teacher Confucius:
If I am walking with two other men, each of them will serve as my teacher.
So he handed Frank the whisk and watched. Smooth as a calm pool.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: TWO STUFFINGS
segments.quote: What is patriotism but the love of the food one ate as a child?
segments.author: Lin Yutang
lines: Lamar made two stuffings: Chicago sausage, and his mom's Memphis cornbread. The table started arguing.
Lamar thought of the Chinese writer Lin Yutang, who asked:
What is patriotism but the love of the food one ate as a child?
So he laughed and made one rule: everybody tries both. Frank had thirds of the cornbread.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: A GOOD ENDING
segments.quote: A hard beginning maketh a good ending.
segments.author: John Heywood
lines: After the pie, Frank stood up. Not bad, Lamar. First time he ever used his name.
Then he raised his root beer with an old saying from John Heywood:
A hard beginning maketh a good ending.
They washed every dish together. Next year, Frank brings the gravy.

segments.head: GOOD NIGHT
segments.quote: Ask. Try. Be kind. Learn. Share. Finish well.
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: So, ask for help, try something, be kind first, learn from anyone, share the table, and trust a hard beginning.
Me? I hosted Thanksgiving once. The smoke alarm got more compliments than I did.
Happy Thanksgiving. I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
